findings.printedLatin: Et ad Hebraeos: « Patres, inquit, quidem carnis nostrae habuimus eruditores et reverebamur eos: non multo magis obtemperabimus patri Spirituum et vivemus et illi quidem in tempore paucorum dierum, secundum voluntatem suam erudiebant nos: hic autem ad id, quod utile est in recipiendo sanctificationem ejus.
findings.englishAsRendered: And to the Hebrews: « We have had, he says, indeed the fathers of our flesh as instructors, and we reverenced them: we shall not much more obey the Father of spirits, and we shall live; and they indeed for a time of few days instructed us according to their own will; but he unto that which is useful, in the receiving of his sanctification.
findings.conjecture: Heb 12:9 is a rhetorical question (*non multo magis obtemperabimus … et vivemus?*, a fortiori). Migne prints the received words exactly but points the clause with a colon and no interrogative mark; rendered flat, the printed `non` becomes a flat denial. Conjecture: Migne's colon stands for a lost question mark.
findings.whyContradiction: Rabanus adduces the verse to establish that 'fathers' means teachers who must be heeded — his own frame a few lines earlier reads *doctores legis et praedicatores Evangelii … quorum doctrinis et exemplis potest homo ad intelligentiam divinam proficere*, and the paired 1 Cor 4:15 citation makes the same point. An assertion that 'we shall not much more obey the Father of spirits' supports nothing in the argument, and its own trailing clause *et vivemus* is incoherent as the consequence of not obeying.
findings.reconciliation: Found blind, then matched to cruces.md @1136C ('Heb. 12:9, and it needs Wilson') and the 'Cruces of construction' entry. Already escalated: Pattern 8 keeps the flat rendering, the crux tested question-mark density in this work empirically, and an OPEN question for Wilson proposes marking such lapses on the page. No new action from this sweep — confirms the class independently.
